A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same study. All 26 pages of each version, including appendices, are readable, and the experiments, figures, and tables can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations, corpus counts, synthetic-relation fine-tuning experiments, and human-checked context experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results, including appendix benchmark and model-size comparisons, and adds statistical comparisons for context effects.

M1.justification: Pairwise yes/no prompting, ten-response voting, and LoRA fine-tuning with correct, reversed, and negated synthetic relations are retained. The new Methodology section reorganizes the approach without introducing a new model, objective, or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six causal graphs, ConceptNet, CauseNet, Dolma/ROOTS corpora, synthetic relations, and positive/negative context scenarios. No additional dataset, domain, or generalization test is introduced.

E2.justification: The same six LLMs participate in the benchmark and context comparisons. Appendix model-size comparisons retain the same Llama2/Llama3 variants and GPT comparators; added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported retrieval protocol narrows from exact, ordered, and embedding-based retrieval in v1 Section 3.3 to exact and ordered string queries in v2 Section 4.3. The corpus-count comparison becomes exact-match-only, although ordered-query performance plots remain. Other evaluation and training settings are retained; rerunning experiments is not established.

E4.justification: v2 removes checks comparing corpus counts across retrieval methods, including embedding thresholds 0.9 and 0.95, and the accompanying direction-confusion analysis. Synthetic scaling, context sensitivity, demonstration-count comparisons, and model-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 adds paired t-tests at p < 0.05 for positive/negative contexts versus no context. Correlation significance reporting and ten generated responses per query already appear in v1; no increase in repetitions is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds aggregate affirmative ratios and significance outcomes, and Figure 1(a) newly marks its Pearson correlation significant. v1 Table 17's ordered-search and embedding-retrieval counts are removed from v2 Table 16. Retained benchmark and model-size scores are identical; reduced numerical precision elsewhere does not establish performance changes.

T1.justification: Task definitions, response-to-label conversion, occurrence ratios, and the NHD-ratio construction are retained. The renamed affirmative measures and expanded background provide explanations without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central findings about frequency, conflicting relations, and context remain. v2's abstract and introduction additionally assert limited generalization to rare or novel causal relations and drop v1's broad claim to the first comprehensive analysis, refining the contribution toward reliability.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the interpretation of retained evidence: limited generalization motivates combining statistical methods with LLMs, conflicting information motivates data cleaning, and negative contexts motivate avoiding misleading inputs. Appendix B.2 adds that most incorrect matches occur in questions or negations, while v1's embedding-retrieval limitation and diagnostic discussion disappear.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents WordNet synonym handling and replaces the anonymous code/data link with a named GitHub repository. It removes the embedding-retrieval query listing. The search window, decoding settings, hardware, and LoRA hyperparameters were already documented; newly implemented synonym handling is not established.

R1.justification: Related work adds references including Feng et al. (2023, 2025), Nick et al. (2023), Jiang et al. (2024), and Cai et al. (2024), while several hybrid-discovery and embedding references disappear. Background expands the distinction between statistical discovery and textual causal knowledge, but the principal research positioning remains similar.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and background are extensively rewritten. v2 adds a dedicated Methodology section, reorganizes hypotheses into research questions with discussions, moves related work into the main text, and moves the correct-versus-incorrect frequency discussion into the appendix.

P2.justification: The same figures are retained with relocation, resizing, and caption edits. Table 1 becomes a compact affirmative-only table with averages and significance markers. The corpus-count table is simplified, the obsolete retrieval-query table is removed, and appendix tables are renumbered and reflowed.

improvement.justification: The dedicated Methodology section, clearer research-question structure, and Table 1 paired tests improve accessibility and statistical reporting. However, v2 removes retrieval checks relevant to its memorization interpretation while making stronger generalization and misleading-context claims from essentially unchanged experiments. These benefits and losses leave the net effect on paper quality uncertain.
